prs.title: fix(bindings): name the Python root package's public surface in __all__
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #586. A PEP 561 marker changes what counts as *exported*, not only whether the package is typed. `offline_protocol_sdk/__init__.py` re-exported the eleven hand-written managers as `from .x import Y  # noqa: F401`, with no `__all__` and no `as Y` alias, and under PEP 561 a type checker treats those as private. So with the marker alone, on the README's own quick start (`from offline_protocol_sdk import ProtocolManager`):

```
# pyright 1.1.407, default mode
app.py:2:34 - error: "ProtocolManager" is not exported from module "offline_protocol_sdk"
    Import from "offline_protocol_sdk.protocol_manager" instead (reportPrivateImportUsage)

# mypy 2.4.0 --strict
app.py:2: error: Module "offline_protocol_sdk" does not explicitly export attribute "ProtocolManager"  [attr-defined]
```

Before the marker both accepted it, since pyright reads an untyped library's source. Pyright is what Pylance runs, so this is the first thing a VS Code user sees after upgrading. The generated names were never affected: `from .offline_protocol import *` is a wildcard import and the generated module defines `__all__`.

This PR:

- lists the root package's public surface in `__all__`: the generated module's own `__all__` plus the eleven managers, using only the `+=` forms the typing spec requires every checker to read;
- adds `bindings/python/tests/test_public_surface.py`, which pins `__all__` to the attributes the package exposes (non-underscore, non-module), so a manager added to the root without a line in `__all__` fails in CI rather than in a user's editor;
- adds the refusal case to `scripts/tests/test-build-wheel.sh` for a package without the marker, which #586 had checked by hand;
- extends the #586 changelog entry.

## Related issues

Refs #586.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix`: bug fix
- [x] `test`: adding or correcting tests

## Checklist

- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated (Unreleased, Fixed; extends the #586 entry)
- No Rust, UDL or binding-generation change, so the cargo gates and binding regeneration don't apply.

## Breaking changes

None at runtime. `from offline_protocol_sdk import *` in an application now brings in exactly the names in `__all__`; before, it also brought in the submodule names (`secure_storage`, `protocol_manager`, ...) that the package's own imports bind. Those stay reachable as attributes.

## Notes for reviewers

How I verified it:

- Built the wheel from this branch, installed it in a clean venv, and ran pyright 1.1.407 and mypy 2.4.0 `--strict` on a consumer doing the README's imports from the root: both pass with full types, and the only reported error is the consumer's intentional wrong-argument call. The same consumer against the #586 wheel shows the four `reportPrivateImportUsage` and `attr-defined` errors above.
- The whole Python suite against this branch: 1128 passed, 4 skipped. The new guard fails on a copy with one name removed from `__all__` and names it (`missing from __all__: ['BleManager']`).
- `scripts/tests/test-build-wheel.sh` on Linux (python:3.12-bookworm, aarch64): all checks pass, including the new "a package without the PEP 561 marker is refused". `shellcheck --severity=warning` is clean on it.

prs.title: fix: the volume-test fixes (ACK ceiling, false send failures, forward-window re-key, BLE queue discards)
prs.body:
Draft. Seven device runs of the two-phone volume test (iPhone 11 and Galaxy M36, 5,000 DMs each way at 5 msg/s over BLE) drove this branch. Run 7, on the head commit with the three review fixes, delivered and acknowledged **10,000 of 10,000**.

## Device runs

| Run | Build | Delivered | What it showed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | main | 70.6% | Engine wedged at 1,000 pending ACKs; `sendMessage` failed sends already on the wire; Android went deaf past the forward window; BLE queues tore large messages |
| 2 | first fixes | 44.8% | Wedge and false failures gone; one-way iOS write stall for 17 min; resends burned ratchet keys |
| 3 | re-seal budget, stall teardown | 58.2% | iOS sent to a stale identifier after Android rotated its address |
| 4 | link resolution, pull mark | 70.5% | Congestion collapse: no per-peer flow control, ACKs queued behind data |
| 5 | window, ACK lane, coalesced ACKs | 50.0% | Flow control held (first 1,800 each way at 100%, ACK RTT about 760 ms); a 10-min outage from two LL links between the same radios |
| 6 | one link per pair, outbox admission | 94.6% | iPhone to Android 5,000/5,000; Android to iPhone 4,460, limited by the indication-only egress at exactly the offered load |
| 7 | review fixes (e8bc81e8) | **100%** | 10,000/10,000 delivered and acknowledged; 0 duplicates, 0 decrypt failures, 0 peers lost, 0 write-stall teardowns (run 6 had 4); about 50 retries per side; ACK RTT p50 under 1 s, p90 17 to 34 s from window holding at the offered load |

## What changed

**Engine**
- A frame is never transmitted without an ACK slot. At the ceiling a send is held and reported as `message_deferred` (`ack_capacity`). `process()` runs every step on every tick. Two leaks that kept the table full are fixed.
- `sendMessage` no longer reports failure for a message it sent.
- A receiver past the forward window re-keys (`TooDistantInTheFuture` is `SessionDesync`; authenticated, so R2 is unchanged). The OpenMLS window rises to 8,192.
- Per-peer window: at most 16 frames awaiting ACK to one peer over a mesh link; the rest are held (`message_deferred`, `peer_window`) and sent in order. Session control is never held.
- BLE queues an ACK ahead of data. Delivery ACKs to a peer advertising `ack_versions` entry 2 are coalesced, up to 5 per frame within 500 ms (`ack_more`).
- Re-seal budget: resends re-seal only while fewer than 256 frames are sealed past the last ACK, then go verbatim; a verbatim copy that can no longer decrypt is re-sealed up to 512. Both derive from the smallest receiver window, a leaf's 1,024, which mls-rs fixes and `tools/mls-interop` pins.
- A frame still in the BLE transport queue gets a bounded ACK extension instead of a retry.
- Outbox admission: a full outbox refuses the newest message to the recipient with the largest backlog. A lighter recipient evicts from the heaviest one (its newest held message first, else its oldest entry). A message awaiting its ACK is never evicted.
- A message sent during a block is never delivered.

**Bridges**
- Outbound fragment queues: cap 768, pull stops at 32 fragments, checked before the destructive pop and only for recipients with a link.
- iOS: a link refusing every write for 15 s is torn down; a foreground connect is cancelled at 10 s, bound to its own attempt; the stall clock is forgotten on connect and disconnect; sends go to the connected identifier after an address rotation; a departed peer is not redialled forever.
- One BLE link per peer pair (ADR 0030): no peer is reported lost while it has another live link (a subscribed central counts only while heard from in the last minute); Android refuses a client link beside a subscribed server link; Android's forced refresh keeps the advertisement while an identified peer is linked unless it has stopped. iOS eviction drops every identifier of the peer.
- Android's indication path drains on confirmation; a failed indication is logged and paced.

**Demo app**: shows the lock for restored sessions.

## Review fixes (last three commits)

- `fix(protocol): let a full outbox evict never-sent held messages`: one slow live peer could make every send to every other recipient a refusal.
- `fix(protocol): size the re-seal budget for the leaf's receiver window`: the budget assumed an 8,192 window that a leaf (mls-rs, fixed at 1,024) does not have.
- `fix(bindings): stop the BLE bridges stalling and flapping peers`: the global backed-up stop, the connect-timer binding, the redial loop, the stall clock, the stale-subscription gate, `evictPeer`, and the Android refresh. A Rust guard now pins this wiring.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --lib` and `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` pass; each of the three review commits passes the unit tests on its own. `offline-protocol-sealed` lints clean on `thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf`.
- `tools/mls-interop` passes, including the two new leaf-window steps; with the constant set to 1,025 it fails.
- The new bridge-wiring guard fails when the connect timer is unbound.
- Swift: the three policy suites pass 39 of 39, and the iOS bridge type-check exits 0.
- Android: 701 of 711 pass from a copy outside the checkout; the 10 failures are `PeerStreamFramingTest`, which cannot find its vector file there.

**Still owed:** a three-device leg for the cross-recipient stall the two-phone harness cannot exercise. Open follow-ups: the iOS write-stall trigger (none fired in run 7), Android's indication-only egress ceiling, and the iPhone's futile dials to Android's rotating advertising address: the stack changed it 9 times in run 7 although the forced refresh kept the advertisement, and the iPhone timed out 92 dials to those addresses while already linked (no effect on delivery).

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` passes
- [ ] `cargo-deny` is satisfied (no dependency changes; not run locally)
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] Docs / `CHANGELOG.md` updated where relevant
- [x] No new `unsafe` in core crates
- [x] The UniFFI UDL did not change
